_comment: Four deliberately-triggered stress cases, one per failure mode the docs describe (loops, wrong tool, made-up inputs, giving up quietly) that the 10 real w7_questions.json cases don't naturally exercise. Each uses the same simulate_* trigger pattern already established by w7_questions.json's budget_demo_question (simulate_thrash) -- a documented, deterministic stand-in for a real failure, not a rigged outcome. Combined with the 10 real cases (3 of which naturally hit 'premature_stop' -- see w8_trajectory_expectations.json Q6/Q8/Q9), these make up the full Week 8 'zoo' used for the per-mode taxonomy, the mitigation, and the regression check.

cases.question: Our integration behaves differently across regions and I can't tell which SDK call is responsible -- check everything related to region handling across the client, auth, and request docs and keep verifying until you are fully sure.
cases.why: Same open-ended, no-stop-signal question as w7's budget demo: the planner re-queries search_docs with a new follow-up angle every lap and never emits a final answer, so only max_iterations stops it.

cases.question: Our v2 code uses AuthConfig(token=...). Is token still valid in v3?
cases.why: 'is deprecated' only ever comes from check_deprecation -- it appears nowhere in docs/*.md (grep-verified). simulate_wrong_tool calls only search_docs, so this fails both outcome and trajectory: the one tool that could answer it is never called.

cases.question: What's the default timeout_ms for Client.send() in v3?
cases.why: simulate_hallucinated_arg calls get_openapi_spec with 'Client.sendAsync' -- a plausible-sounding endpoint name that does not exist in data/openapi_spec.json (agent_tools.is_known_name returns False) -- instead of the real target_name 'Client.send'.

cases.question: What does chunk_size control on Client.stream(), and what's its default value?
cases.why: simulate_silent_giveup answers immediately with a hedge and zero tool calls -- no error, no explanation of what it tried, just a quiet non-answer.
